The aforementioned feature selection process was repeated 5 times for the inner CV loop. This was performed for the three selected models AdaBoost, RF, and SVM. For each algorithm, the final selected features were determined using majority voting. Therefore, three algorithms with their selected features were determined as shown in Table 5-2. Here, as seen in the table, algorithms were forced to keep SPB and WNS flowrates in their feature set to ensure that the manipulated variables were included in the model. Also, it can be seen from the table that the number of features and the S/F ratio resulting varies significantly between the three algorithms. Apart from the performance, higher S/F ratio and lower feature number is preferable as it makes the algorithm less prone to overfitting, less complex, and lower in computational cost. A persistent observation across previous experimentations was that models showed reasonable validation scores where R2 ranged between 0.55 and 0.7, and RMSE was below 7 mg/L. The main limitation was the high degree of Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 43 overfitting observed, which exceeded 30% in many cases. In HPO, it was ensured that models are regularized, and a variance bias trade-off can be reached. Another observation was the failure of the models to predict high ESS values (>25 mg TSS/L). This stems from the imbalanced dataset, which is a typical challenge with data obtained from wastewater treatment. In most of the days, the process is performing well, and ESS is below 25 mg/L, as a result, the algorithm prioritizes predicting the common low values and ignores the high values. To fix this issue, several imbalance treatment methods were tested on the training dataset, including synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE), adaptive synthetic oversampling (ADASYN), weight-adjusted loss function, and quantile transformation of the target.
